title: Cycle Surge & Rebalance — dynamic staffing, rapid reprioritization, and rolling scope decisions
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Problem: mid-cycle shifts (urgent customer escalations, infra incidents, sudden regulatory asks) frequently force ad-hoc staffing moves and scope cuts that lack transparent decision criteria. Goals: (1) provide a lightweight, repeatable runbook for rebalancing teams mid-cycle; (2) define quantitative allocation targets and threshold triggers for surge lanes; (3) produce a simple prioritization rubric to guide scope cuts that preserve roadmap outcomes with minimum customer/regulatory risk. Deliverables: a one-page runbook, a triage matrix (impact x effort x risk), a recommended staffing reallocation template, and a short automation script to compute available capacity from cycle-level JIRA/Linear estimates.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook doc exists and is reviewed by Eng, Design, and SRE
Triage matrix and prioritization rubric documented with example application to 2 live initiatives
Staffing reallocation template shared and used in one simulated drill
Automation script returns plausible available capacity numbers for current cycle and is in the repo with README
decisions: Use a 3-tier surge model: Local (team-level), Cross-team (within product org), and Central (exec-assisted)
Reserve 8% of cycle capacity as baseline surge buffer; additional surge requires exec approval with customer justification
Scope cuts prioritized by 'customer impact severity' then 'strategic dependency', not purely by effort
tradeoffs: Higher baseline surge buffer reduces planned delivery headcount but improves responsiveness to incidents
Automated capacity estimates increase speed but rely on reasonably accurate point estimates from teams
Rigid rules speed decisions but reduce team autonomy for creative tradeoffs
runbook_steps: 1) Trigger: Incident/escalation/priority change logged and tagged 'surge-candidate' in Linear
2) Triage (within 6 hours): PM + Eng TL + SRE estimate customer impact and required urgency
3) Compute available capacity: run automation script to get remaining story points and 'reserved surge' pool
4) Decide level: If impact=critical and remaining capacity < required -> escalate to Cross-team; if greater than cross-team threshold -> exec-assisted
5) Rebalance: propose reassignments, list explicit scope cuts (must be ticket-level), communicate to stakeholders
6) Execute and monitor: 72-hour check-in, adjust as needed, and produce retrospective note
example_calculation: Example: Cycle has 1200 team story points. Baseline reserve = 8% => 96 pts. Current consumption=980 pts. Available pool = 1200 - 980 - 96 = 124 pts. Urgent customer patch estimated 40 pts => local reassignments possible. If urgent ask = 200 pts, cross-team surge needed (requires approvals).
